clues: This is the capital of Turkey. It sits in the middle of the land, and it is its second biggest city.
It sits in one of the driest parts of Turkey, ringed by dry grass steppe. Yet it counts as a green city, with much park land per person.
In 1923 it became the new capital of Turkey. It took that role from Istanbul when the old empire fell.
This city gave its name to soft wool from rabbits. The same name fits a long-haired goat and a fluffy cat.
A rocky hill crowns its old centre, topped by the ruins of an old castle. A river runs just below that hill.
